name: Number of primes of the form n - 2^k.
comment: Erdős conjectures that the numbers in A039669 are the only n for which n-2^r is prime for all 1<2^r<n. - _T. D. Noe_ and _Robert G. Wilson v_, Jul 19 2005 [Edited by _Bernard Schott_, Jun 26 2026]
link: T. D. Noe, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..10000
Erdős problems database contributors, Erdős problem database, see no. 236.
formula: G.f.: ( Sum_{i>=0} x^(2^i) ) * ( Sum_{j>=1} x^prime(j) ). - _Ilya Gutkovskiy_, Feb 10 2022
example: 127 is the smallest odd number > 1 such that a(n) = 0: A006285(2) = 127. - _Reinhard Zumkeller_, May 27 2015
mathematica: Table[cnt=0; r=1; While[r<n, If[PrimeQ[n-r], cnt++ ]; r=2r]; cnt, {n, 150}] (* _T. D. Noe_, Jul 19 2005 *)
f[n_] := Count[ PrimeQ[n - 2^Range[0, Floor[ Log[2, n]]]], True]; Table[ f[n], {n, 105}] (* _Robert G. Wilson v_, Jul 21 2005 *)
program: (Magma) a109925:=function(n); count:=0; e:=1; while e le n do if IsPrime(n-e) then count+:=1; end if; e*:=2; end while; return count; end function; [ a109925(n): n in [1..105] ]; // _Klaus Brockhaus_, Oct 30 2010
a109925 n = sum $ map (a010051' . (n -)) $ takeWhile (< n)  a000079_list
def A109925(n): return sum(1 for i in range(n.bit_length()) if isprime(n-(1<<i))) # _Chai Wah Wu_, Nov 29 2023
